questions.q: What does a Stream actually store?
options: Nothing — it recomputes change history from table backups each time
A full duplicate copy of the entire source table
An offset marking where it last left off, not a copy of the changed rows
A compressed archive of every row ever deleted
questions.explain: A Stream stores an offset and computes changes on demand from Snowflake's change-tracking metadata, rather than storing a copy of the data itself.

questions.q: What has to happen for a Stream's offset to move forward?
options: 24 hours must pass since the Stream was created
A DML statement that references the Stream must successfully commit
The underlying warehouse must be resized
Any SELECT against the Stream, even on its own
questions.explain: Only a committing DML statement that references the Stream advances its offset — a standalone SELECT does not.

questions.q: What does METADATA$ACTION report on a row returned by a Stream?
options: The exact timestamp the row was first created
Whether that row represents an INSERT or a DELETE
Which warehouse processed the change
The row's physical storage location
questions.explain: METADATA$ACTION is one of the Stream's automatic metadata columns, reporting INSERT or DELETE for each returned row.

options: The full contents of the Stream as a JSON array
The exact number of rows currently in the Stream
The name of the table the Stream is attached to
TRUE or FALSE, depending on whether the Stream currently has unconsumed changes
questions.explain: SYSTEM$STREAM_HAS_DATA is a boolean check, used in Lesson 6's Task so it only runs when there's genuinely something new.

questions.q: Why is it safe to run SELECT * FROM tickets_stream as many times as you like while exploring?
options: A standalone SELECT, with no other DML in the same transaction, does not advance the Stream's offset
SELECT statements against a Stream are read from a separate, disposable copy
It isn't safe — each SELECT consumes the Stream's current contents
Streams automatically reset their offset every hour regardless of what queries run
questions.explain: Only a committing DML statement moves the offset forward, so a plain SELECT can be re-run freely without consuming anything.
